g9-economics-ue3-t1.overview: Types of Resources and Factor Payments sits inside Economic Resources and Markets. Economic resources and the markets that trade them are the focus of Unit 3 of Grade 9 Economics in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it sorts resources into land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship, each with its own factor payment. Then it separates renewable from non-renewable resources and explains conservation. Next, it looks at the goods, labour, and financial markets, and traces the circular flow of income. Finally, it examines land as a key resource in Ethiopia. Students will also learn how economic resources support real-life production and trade.
objectives: Classify economic resources into land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship.
Match each factor of production with its factor payment.
Distinguish renewable from non-renewable resources.
Compare the goods, labour, and financial markets.
Draw and interpret the two-sector and three-sector circular flow models.
g9-economics-ue3-t1.simple:
Types of Resources and Factor Payments in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the difference between free resources and economic (scarce) resources.
  • Then the four categories: land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship.
  • Also the factor payment for each: rent, wages, interest, and profit.
g9-economics-ue3-t1.detailed:
Types of Resources and Factor Payments — the essentials. First, the difference between free resources and economic (scarce) resources. Then the four categories: land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship. Also the factor payment for each: rent, wages, interest, and profit.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Classify economic resources into land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship.
  • Match each factor of production with its factor payment.
  • Distinguish renewable from non-renewable resources.
  • Compare the goods, labour, and financial markets.
  • Draw and interpret the two-sector and three-sector circular flow models.
